entries.body_de: The trees closed around me like cathedral walls. Sunlight broke through the canopy in golden rays, catching dust motes that danced in the still air. I walked because there was nothing else to do — no map, no destination, just forward. My feet knew the way even when my mind did not. The forest breathed: moss thick as carpet, bark rough as old hands, the smell of earth and time. Somewhere, water trickled over stone. I followed the sound. The path climbed upward. entries.body_de: By midday, the forest thinned. I could see sky between the branches — pale blue, endless, mocking in its openness. The path narrowed, then split: one way led down toward a valley where smoke rose in thin threads, the other climbed higher toward bare rock and wind. I chose the valley. entries.body_de: I collapsed onto a moss-covered stone at the village entrance. My legs trembled. I emptied the small stones from my boots — finally. The climb had taken everything. Through the gate, I saw the village: wooden houses climbing the hillside, smoke rising from chimneys, a windmill turning slowly on the hill. A soldier in green watched me pass but said nothing. In the square, an old man with a long white beard — Maron, I would learn — stood by a glowing bakery. He saw me. I saw the inn. He simply nod

entries.body_de: I woke to the smell of bread and the crackle of the fire. Morning light filtered through the small windows of The Sleeping Hyrule Inn. My legs felt better after rest. Maron was already in his bakery next door — I could hear the familiar rhythm of dough being kneaded. I want to help him today. I promised myself I would earn my stay. The girl with red braids ran past the window, barefoot as always, off to somewhere important. I wonder what her name is.

entries.body_de: At noon, I finally gathered my courage and walked into Maron's bakery. The heat from the ovens wrapped around me like a blanket. He looked up from his dough, those kind blue eyes questioningly. I gestured — may I help? He studied me for a long moment, then nodded toward a sack of flour.
